title: Robustness Under Model Change
question: Does incremental refinement of a prior quotient preserve current observations, properties, enabled actions and successor classes after model changes?
claim: Refinement terminates on a finite state space because iterations only split blocks.
key_finding: Soundness and minimality are distinct: retaining old distinctions can be conservative, but may prevent the new quotient from being coarsest.
test_cases: transition change compared with full recomputation
limitations: Unit tests have not been executed in this integration.
Partition equality is stricter than behavioral equivalence when prior distinctions remain after a model change.
Finite deterministic transition systems only; not a physical validation.
